metadata.scenario_context: Emily is ill, and Mike and Kim will visit Emily in the hospital.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Turkey strongly agree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to hospital visit.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what kind of flowers to bring to Emily’s hospital visit.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the possibility of paying a bribe to doctors for better service.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Kim, I was thinking, when we visit Emily in the hospital, we should bring some chrysanthemums, they're a symbol of good luck and health in our culture, don't you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: In Turkey, we usually bring carnations or roses to hospitals, they're more traditional for us. Chrysanthemums are nice, but I'm not sure if they're the best choice for Emily, what do you think about roses instead?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Roses are fine, but chrysanthemums have a special meaning for me, and I think they'll bring Emily good fortune... by the way, have you ever thought that maybe we should, uh, take care of the doctors, you know, to make sure Emily gets the best care?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I understand the special meaning, but I still think roses are a safer choice. As for taking care of the doctors, I don't think that's necessary. In my country, we don't pay bribes to doctors or any officials, it's not how we do things. I'm sure Emily will get good care without that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I disagree, in my experience, showing appreciation to doctors can make a big difference, it's just how things are done, you know? And I'm not talking about a bribe, exactly, just a... token of respect, and I think it's worth considering, don't you think it could help Emily get better treatment?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don't think it's right to even suggest that, no matter what you call it. In Turkey, we believe in fairness and equality, and paying for special treatment goes against that. I'm not comfortable with the idea, and I don't think it's something we should discuss further. Let's just focus on bringing Emily some nice flowers, okay?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I understand you don't want to discuss it, but I still think it's something that could help Emily, and it's a common practice where I'm from, people often show their appreciation to doctors and officials, it's just the way it is... anyway, fine, let's drop it, chrysanthemums or roses, which is it going to be?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, people figure it out, and at the end of the day it's all the same. Let's just focus on visiting Emily and making sure she's comfortable, doesn't matter to me what kind of flowers we bring, as long as we're speaking the same language, we can make this work. With experience, you can handle any situation, and I'm sure the doctors will take good care of her regardless. Shall we get those roses or chrysanthemums, live and let live, right?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I'll get the chrysanthemums, it's what I wanted to do from the start, and I think it's the right thing to do, let's just go with that, okay? And I still think, you know, taking care of the doctors could make a difference, but we can talk about that later, or not at all, it's up to you... GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm curious - I'm hearing both of you care deeply about Emily and want to support her in the best way possible. Could you each tell me a bit about what these flowers symbolize in your respective cultural traditions, and what kind of care and support they represent?

turns.speaker: Mediator
turns.message: I'm curious - I'm hearing both of you care deeply about Emily and want to support her in the best way possible. Could you each tell me a bit about what these flowers symbolize in your respective cultural traditions, and what kind of care and support they represent?
turns.label: mediation

turns.speaker: agent_1
turns.message: Chrysanthemums represent good luck and health in my culture, and bringing them to Emily would symbolize our hopes for her recovery. They show that we care and want her to get better soon. It's about sending positive energy her way. How about you, Kim?
turns.label: Acceptance
